title: Spatchcocked Roast Chicken with Garlic Pan Juices
description: A flattened whole chicken roasts in under an hour with crisp skin and juicy meat, then the drippings simmer with roasted garlic, lemon, and broth into simple pan juices.
notes: For the crispiest skin, season the chicken and refrigerate it uncovered on a plate for 8 to 24 hours before roasting. Resting time (10 to 15 minutes) is not included in the cook time. Plan on roughly 12 minutes per pound for a flattened bird at this temperature; a 5 lb chicken needs about 10 minutes longer, but always go by the thermometer rather than the clock. Do not rinse raw chicken, and wash the shears, board, and your hands with hot soapy water after handling it. Broth is usually gluten-free but check the label. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 4 days; reheat to 165°F. Save the backbone and carcass for stock.

ingredients.name: large yellow onion, cut into 1/2-inch-thick rounds

instructions: Set the chicken breast-side down on a cutting board without rinsing it. Using kitchen shears, cut along both sides of the backbone and remove it, then turn the bird over and press hard on the breastbone with the heel of your hand until it cracks and the chicken lies flat. Pat the skin very dry with paper towels.

Mix the salt, pepper, and paprika. Loosen the skin over the breasts and thighs with your fingers and rub about a third of the seasoning directly onto the meat, then rub the rest over the skin and the underside. Let the chicken sit at room temperature for up to 30 minutes while the oven heats.

Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the upper-middle position. Arrange the onion rounds, garlic halves (cut side down), thyme, and lemon halves (cut side down) in the center of the skillet or roasting pan and pour in 1/4 cup of the broth. Lay the chicken skin-side up on top, tuck the wing tips behind the breasts, and rub the skin with the olive oil.

Roast for 45 to 55 minutes, rotating the pan once halfway through, until the skin is deep golden and crisp and a thermometer reads 165°F in the thickest part of the breast and at least 175°F in the thigh, not touching bone. If the drippings start to look dark and dry before the chicken is done, add a few tablespoons of water to the pan.

Move the chicken to a cutting board and let it rest, uncovered, for 10 to 15 minutes. Squeeze the soft garlic cloves out of their skins into the pan, discard the skins and thyme stems, and set the lemon halves aside.

Spoon off all but about 1 tablespoon of fat from the pan, keeping the onions and browned bits (the handle will be very hot). Set the pan over medium heat, add the remaining 3/4 cup broth, and simmer for 4 to 5 minutes, scraping the bottom and mashing the garlic, until the liquid has reduced by about half and looks lightly syrupy. Squeeze in the juice of one roasted lemon half, then taste and add a pinch of salt if needed.

Carve the chicken into legs, thighs, wings, and breast pieces, and pour any juices from the board into the pan. Spoon the pan juices and onions over the chicken, sprinkle with parsley if using, and serve with the remaining lemon half for squeezing.

title: Smoky Chicken Tinga Tacos
description: Tender shredded chicken simmered with softened onions in a smoky tomato-chipotle sauce, piled into warm corn tortillas with avocado, cilantro, and lime.
notes: Heat level: use 2 chipotles for mild and 4 for spicy. Chicken breasts also work; poach them for 12 to 15 minutes, until 165°F. The tinga keeps for 4 days in the refrigerator or 3 months in the freezer, and the flavor improves overnight; refrigerate within 2 hours and reheat to 165°F with a splash of water. It is also good on tostadas or over rice. Corn tortillas and canned chipotles are usually gluten-free, but some brands contain wheat, so check labels if that matters to you. The recipe as written is dairy-free; crumbled cotija or a spoonful of crema is a traditional topping if you eat dairy.

ingredients.name: chipotle peppers in adobo sauce, plus 1 tbsp sauce from the can
large white onion, halved and thinly sliced

instructions: Put the chicken (do not rinse it), 2 of the garlic cloves, the bay leaves, and 1 teaspoon of the salt in a medium saucepan and cover with 4 cups of cold water. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce the heat to low, partially cover, and simmer gently for 15 to 18 minutes, until the chicken reads at least 165°F in the thickest part and pulls apart easily.
Lift the chicken onto a plate and reserve 3/4 cup of the poaching liquid. When the chicken is cool enough to handle, shred it with two forks.

Blend the tomatoes with their juices, the chipotles and adobo sauce, the remaining 2 garlic cloves, the oregano, the cumin, and 1/2 cup of the reserved poaching liquid for about 30 seconds, until smooth.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and cook, stirring often, for 8 to 10 minutes, until soft and golden at the edges.

Carefully pour in the sauce (it will spatter) and simmer over medium-low heat for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until it darkens and thickens enough that a spoon dragged across the pan leaves a trail for a moment.

Stir in the shredded chicken and cook for about 5 minutes, until the chicken has absorbed some of the sauce and the mixture is juicy but not soupy. Loosen with the remaining poaching liquid if it looks dry, then taste and adjust the salt.

Warm the tortillas one or two at a time in a dry skillet over medium-high heat for about 30 seconds per side, until pliable and lightly toasted. Fill with the tinga and top with avocado, cilantro, and a squeeze of lime.

title: Sheet-Pan Chicken Shawarma with Garlic Yogurt Sauce
description: Chicken thighs marinated in lemon, garlic, and warm spices roast on one pan with red onion until charred at the edges, then get sliced thin and served with a cool garlic yogurt sauce.
notes: Marinating time (1 to 8 hours) is not included in the prep time. Always marinate in the refrigerator, and do not go past 8 hours: the lemon juice starts to make the surface of the chicken mushy. Discard any marinade left in the bowl. Chicken breasts can be used; roast for 18 to 22 minutes, to 165°F. Serve with chopped cucumber, tomato, and pickles. For a gluten-free meal, skip the pita and serve over rice or salad. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 4 days; the sauce keeps for 4 days and the garlic gets stronger as it sits.

ingredients.name: large red onion, cut into 1/2-inch wedges

instructions: Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, grated garlic, cumin, paprika, coriander, turmeric, cinnamon, and salt in a large bowl. Add the chicken (do not rinse it) and turn until every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour and up to 8 hours.

Make the sauce by stirring together the yogurt, garlic, lemon juice, and salt, adding 1 to 2 tablespoons of water until it is thick but spoonable. Refrigerate for at least 15 minutes so the raw garlic mellows.

Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the upper third. Add the onion wedges to the bowl with the chicken and toss to coat, then spread everything on a rimmed baking sheet in a single layer, opening the thighs flat. Discard any marinade left in the bowl.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, turning the chicken once halfway through, until the edges are browned and the thickest piece reads at least 165°F (thighs stay juicy up to about 185°F).
Switch the oven to broil on high and broil for 2 to 3 minutes, watching closely, until the chicken and onions are charred in spots.
Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes, then slice it thinly across the grain and toss the slices with the onions and juices on the pan.
Serve the chicken and onions in warm pita or on plates, with the garlic yogurt sauce spooned over the top.

title: From-Scratch Chicken Teriyaki
description: Pan-seared chicken thighs glazed in a four-ingredient sauce of soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar that reduces in the skillet to a glossy coating. Ready in 30 minutes.
notes: The sauce thickens by reduction, so no cornstarch is needed; it will continue to thicken as it cools. If you do not have sake, use water or dry sherry. To make the dish gluten-free, use gluten-free tamari in place of soy sauce and check the mirin label. Leave off the sesame seeds for a sesame-free version. Because the sauce is added after the chicken is cooked through, there is no raw marinade to discard. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 4 days; reheat to 165°F with a splash of water to loosen the glaze.
instructions: Stir the soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, and ginger in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Pat the chicken dry with paper towels without rinsing it, trim any large pieces of fat, and open each thigh flat so it is an even thickness. Sprinkle both sides with the salt.

Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Lay the chicken in the pan smooth side down and cook without moving it for 5 to 6 minutes, until deep golden brown and it releases easily from the pan.
Turn the chicken, lower the heat to medium, and cook for 4 to 5 minutes more, until the thickest part reads 165°F. Tilt the pan and blot up the excess fat with a folded paper towel held in tongs.

Pour in the sauce and simmer over medium heat for 4 to 6 minutes, turning the chicken every minute or so, until the sauce reduces to a glossy syrup with large bubbles that coats the back of a spoon. Take the pan off the heat as soon as it thickens, because the sugars burn quickly.
Rest the chicken on a cutting board for 3 minutes, then slice it into 1/2-inch strips. Serve over the rice with the remaining glaze spooned on top, finished with scallions and sesame seeds if using.

title: Filipino Chicken Adobo
description: Bone-in chicken browned and braised with vinegar, soy sauce, plenty of garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns, then reduced until the sauce is glossy, tangy, and savory. Serve over steamed rice.
equipment: Dutch oven or deep lidded skillet
notes: No salt is added because the soy sauce seasons the dish; taste the reduced sauce before adjusting anything. Filipino cane vinegar is traditional, and coconut, rice, or apple cider vinegar also work. For deeper flavor you can marinate the chicken in the vinegar, soy sauce, and garlic in the refrigerator for up to 12 hours, then pat it dry before browning; the marinade is safe to use as the braising liquid because it is boiled. Use gluten-free tamari to make the dish gluten-free. Adobo tastes even better the next day: refrigerate within 2 hours, keep for up to 4 days, and reheat to 165°F.

ingredients.name: bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks
cane vinegar or distilled white vinegar

instructions: Pat the chicken dry with paper towels without rinsing it. Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat until it shimmers, then brown the chicken skin-side down, in two batches if the pot is crowded, for 5 to 6 minutes, until the skin is golden and has rendered some fat. Turn and cook for 1 minute more, then move the chicken to a plate.
Pour off all but about 1 tablespoon of fat. Lower the heat to medium, add the garlic, and stir for 30 to 60 seconds, until fragrant and pale gold.

Add the vinegar, soy sauce, water, bay leaves, and peppercorns, scraping up the browned bits. Return the chicken, skin-side up, with any juices from the plate. Bring to a boil and let it bubble for 2 minutes without stirring, which cooks off the sharpest edge of the vinegar.

Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer gently for 25 minutes, turning the pieces once halfway through, until the chicken is tender and the thickest thigh reads at least 175°F (165°F is the safe minimum).

Uncover, raise the heat to medium-high, and boil the sauce for 8 to 10 minutes, basting the chicken occasionally, until it has reduced by about half, looks glossy, and lightly coats a spoon. Stir in the brown sugar, if using, during the last minute.

Taste the sauce and add a splash of water if it is too sharp or salty for you. Discard the bay leaves and serve the chicken over the rice with plenty of sauce and garlic spooned on top, sprinkled with scallions if you like.

title: Oven-Roasted Chicken Tikka
description: Bite-size chicken thighs marinated in spiced yogurt with ginger and garlic, roasted hot on a rack and finished under the broiler for charred edges. Serve with sliced onion and lemon.
notes: Marinating time (2 to 12 hours) is not included in the prep time. Marinate in the refrigerator and discard the used marinade. Thick Greek yogurt clings best; if using regular plain yogurt, strain it for 30 minutes first. Pure ground spices are gluten-free, but blends such as garam masala occasionally include fillers, so check the label. Chicken breast works too: roast for 10 to 12 minutes before broiling and pull it at 165°F. The pieces can be threaded onto metal skewers and grilled over medium-high heat for 10 to 12 minutes instead. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 4 days in wraps, salads, or a tomato-based curry sauce.

ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
neutral oil, plus more for the rack
Kashmiri chili powder (or 1 1/2 tsp sweet paprika plus 1/2 tsp cayenne)

instructions: Toss the chicken pieces (do not rinse them) with the lemon juice and salt in a large bowl and let them stand for 10 minutes while you mix the marinade.

Stir the yogurt, oil, ginger, garlic, chili powder, garam masala, cumin, coriander, and turmeric together until smooth, then add to the chicken and mix until every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours and up to 12 hours.
Set an oven rack about 6 inches below the broiler and heat the oven to 450°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with foil, set a wire rack on top, and brush the rack lightly with oil.

Lift the chicken out of the marinade, leaving a thin coating on each piece and wiping off any thick clumps, and arrange the pieces on the rack with a little space between them. Discard the marinade left in the bowl.
Roast for 12 to 15 minutes, turning the pieces once, until the surface looks dry, the edges are starting to brown, and the largest piece reads 165°F.
Switch the oven to broil on high and broil for 2 to 4 minutes, turning once, until the chicken is charred in spots. Watch closely, since the yogurt coating can go from charred to burnt quickly.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes, then serve with the sliced onion, cilantro, and lemon wedges for squeezing.

title: Classic Chicken Parmesan
description: Thin chicken cutlets in a crisp Parmesan-panko crust, topped with a quick garlicky tomato sauce and melted mozzarella, then baked until bubbling and browned.
equipment: rimmed baking sheet with wire rack
notes: Keeping the sauce in a strip down the middle of each cutlet leaves the edges crisp. Throw away any flour, egg, and crumbs left over from breading, since they have touched raw chicken. The cutlets can be breaded up to 4 hours ahead and refrigerated uncovered on a rack. Serve with spaghetti or a green salad and the extra sauce. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 3 days; reheat on a rack in a 375°F oven for 12 to 15 minutes, until 165°F in the center, to bring back some of the crispness.

ingredients.name: large boneless, skinless chicken breasts (about 1 1/2 lb total)
olive oil or neutral oil, for frying

instructions: Make the sauce: warm 1 tablespoon olive oil and the garlic in a small saucepan over medium heat for about 1 minute, until fragrant but not browned. Add the crushed tomatoes and 1/4 teaspoon salt and simmer over medium-low heat for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick enough to mound on a spoon.

Heat the oven to 425°F. Cut each chicken breast in half horizontally to make 4 cutlets, then pound them between sheets of parchment to an even 1/2-inch thickness. Season both sides with 1 teaspoon salt and the pepper.

Set out three shallow dishes: the flour in one, the eggs beaten with 1 tablespoon water in the second, and the panko mixed with 1/2 cup of the Parmesan and the oregano in the third. Coat each cutlet in flour and shake off the excess, dip it in egg, then press it firmly into the crumbs on both sides.

Heat the frying oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until a breadcrumb dropped in sizzles right away (about 350°F). Fry the cutlets two at a time for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until deep golden brown, then move them to a wire rack set in a rimmed baking sheet.
Spoon about 1/4 cup of sauce down the center of each cutlet, leaving the edges bare, and top with the mozzarella and the remaining 1/4 cup Parmesan.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until the cheese is bubbling and browned in spots and the chicken reads 165°F in the thickest part.
Let the cutlets rest for 3 minutes, scatter the basil over the top, and serve with the remaining warm sauce on the side.

title: White Chicken Chili with Green Chiles
description: A lighter chili of shredded chicken, white beans, corn, and mild green chiles in a cumin-scented broth, thickened with mashed beans instead of cream and brightened with lime.
notes: Boneless thighs can replace the breasts; simmer them for about 20 minutes. For more heat, leave the seeds in the jalapeño or add a pinch of cayenne. Broth, canned beans, and canned chiles are normally gluten-free, but check labels if you are cooking for someone with celiac disease. The chili as written is dairy-free; sour cream or shredded Monterey Jack are good toppings if you eat dairy. Refrigerate within 2 hours and keep for up to 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. It thickens as it sits, so reheat to 165°F with a splash of broth or water.

ingredients.name: diced green chiles (4 oz each), undrained
white beans such as cannellini or great northern (15 oz each), drained and rinsed

instructions: Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion and jalapeño and cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 to 6 minutes, until soft and translucent. Stir in the garlic, cumin, oregano, and coriander and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.

Add the broth, green chiles, and salt, then add the chicken (do not rinse it), making sure it is submerged. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer gently for 15 to 18 minutes, until the chicken reads 165°F in the thickest part.
Move the chicken to a plate and shred it with two forks.
While the chicken cools slightly, mash 1 cup of the beans with a fork to a coarse paste. Stir the mashed beans, the remaining whole beans, and the corn into the pot.
Simmer uncovered over medium heat for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until the broth has thickened slightly and looks creamy.
Return the shredded chicken to the pot and heat through for 2 minutes. Take the pot off the heat, stir in the lime juice and cilantro, then taste and add more salt if needed.
Ladle the chili into bowls and top with diced avocado if you like.

title: Crispy Baked Buffalo Wings
description: Oven-baked wings that turn out blistered and crisp without frying, thanks to a light coating of baking powder and a wire rack, tossed in a buttery cayenne hot sauce.
notes: Dairy-free option: replace the butter with 3 tablespoons olive oil or a dairy-free butter; the wings themselves contain no dairy. Use baking powder, not baking soda, and make sure it is labeled gluten-free and aluminum-free (aluminum can leave a metallic taste). Dry skin is the key to crispness: for even better results, arrange the coated wings on the rack and refrigerate uncovered for 8 to 24 hours before baking. Three pounds of split wings is about 30 pieces and serves 4 to 6 as an appetizer. Most cayenne hot sauces are gluten-free, but check the label. Toss the cooked wings in a clean bowl, not the one that held the raw chicken. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 3 days; reheat on a rack at 400°F for 8 to 10 minutes, until 165°F.

ingredients.name: chicken wings, split into flats and drumettes, tips removed
unsalted butter (or olive oil for a dairy-free sauce)

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the upper-middle position. Line a rimmed baking sheet with foil, set a wire rack on top, and rub the rack with the oil.

Pat the wings very dry with paper towels without rinsing them. Mix the baking powder, salt, garlic powder, pepper, and paprika in a large bowl, add the wings, and toss until they are thinly and evenly coated with no powdery patches.
Arrange the wings on the rack skin-side up in a single layer with a little space between them so the hot air can circulate.

Bake for 25 minutes, turn the wings over, and bake for 20 to 25 minutes more, until deep golden brown with blistered, crisp skin. They will be well past the safe minimum of 165°F by this point; wings are at their most tender around 185°F or higher.
During the last 5 minutes of baking, melt the butter in a small saucepan over low heat, then whisk in the hot sauce and honey until smooth and just warm. Do not let it boil or the sauce may separate.
Let the wings rest on the rack for 5 minutes, then transfer them to a clean large bowl, pour the sauce over, and toss to coat. Serve right away with celery sticks if you like.

title: Thai-Inspired Turkey Larb Lettuce Wraps
description: Ground turkey tossed while warm with lime juice, fish sauce, shallots, fresh mint, and toasted rice powder, then spooned into crisp lettuce cups. Bright, savory, and on the table in about 35 minutes.
equipment: mortar and pestle or spice grinder
notes: Larb is traditionally made with chicken or pork; ground turkey is an adaptation, and ground chicken works the same way. The toasted rice powder adds a nutty flavor and a slight crunch and can be made up to a month ahead and kept in a sealed jar. Fish sauce is normally gluten-free but check the label. Start with 1/2 teaspoon of red pepper flakes and add more at the table. Serve with sticky rice or jasmine rice for a fuller meal. Refrigerate the turkey mixture within 2 hours and use within 3 days, adding fresh herbs just before serving; reheat to 165°F.

ingredients.name: red pepper flakes, or more to taste
chopped fresh cilantro leaves and tender stems

instructions: Toast the rice in a dry 12-inch skillet over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 6 to 8 minutes, until deep golden and nutty-smelling. Let it cool for 2 minutes, then grind it to a coarse powder, about the texture of sand, in a mortar or spice grinder.
Stir the lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, and red pepper flakes together in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves.

Wipe out the skillet and heat the oil over medium-high heat. Add the turkey and salt and cook, breaking the meat into small crumbles, for 6 to 8 minutes, until no pink remains, most of the liquid has cooked off, and the turkey reads 165°F.
Take the pan off the heat and let the turkey cool for 2 minutes so the herbs will not wilt. Stir in the dressing, shallots, scallions, and toasted rice powder.
Fold in the mint and cilantro. Taste the mixture, which should be tangy, salty, and lightly spicy, and adjust with a little more lime juice, fish sauce, or red pepper flakes.
Spoon the warm turkey into the lettuce leaves and serve with the cucumber slices alongside.
